Action: Real-time combat or movement challenge is central
Adventure: Story-led exploration and interaction, typically point-and-click or narrative driven
Board Game: Adaptation of, or built like, a tabletop board game
Casual: Short sessions, low stakes, easy to pick up
Coop: Designed to be played cooperatively with other people
Crime: Detective work, investigation or criminal underworld themes
Dating Sim: Relationship-building with characters as the core loop
Deckbuilder: Building a deck of cards during play is the core mechanic
Exploration: Discovering the world at the player's own pace is the point
Historical: Set in a real historical period
Management: Running a system, business, colony or organisation
Mystery: A central mystery to unravel that is not primarily a crime investigation
Platformer: Jumping and traversal across platforms is the core mechanic
Puzzle: Solving puzzles is the core activity
RPG: Role-playing game with character progression and choices
Roguelike: Procedural runs with permadeath or run-based progression
Shooter: Shooting-based action not from a first-person or twin-stick perspective
Simulation: Simulates a real-world activity or system in detail
Social Deduction: Players deduce hidden roles or intentions among themselves
Soulslike: Demanding third-person combat with checkpoint-based death and recovery
Stealth: Avoiding detection is the primary approach
Strategy: Planning and resource decisions over a large scale, often real-time or grand strategy
Survival: Managing hunger, resources or exposure to stay alive
Tactics: Turn-based tactical combat with individual units
Twin-Stick Shooter: Shooting with independent movement and aiming, usually top-down
Visual Novel: Illustrated, text-heavy storytelling with occasional choices
Walking Simulator: First-person exploration and narrative with little or no challenge
Western: Set in the American Old West
